title: Number line to 20
examples: Teacher, if I start at 2 and jump three times, where do I land?
How do I know which number comes right after 17 on the line?

explain.say: Look at the number line on the screen. We are learning about where numbers sit.
The number 7 is in a specific spot. We say its position is seven.
If we count up, the number 10 is further along the line than 5. It is bigger.
Now we learn about jumps. If we start at 3 and jump one space, we land on 4.
Jumping means counting forward by a set amount. From 5, jumping two times gets us to 7.

faq.q: What does it mean to be 'between' two numbers?
faq.a: It means the number that sits right in the middle of those two numbers. For example, 8 is between 7 and 9.
asks: What number is in the middle?
What number comes after 12 and before 14?

faq.q: If I jump backwards, am I counting down?
faq.a: Yes, jumping backwards is like counting down. If you start at 10 and jump back two, you land on 8.
asks: How do I count backwards on the line?

faq.q: Can I jump more than one space at a time?
faq.a: Yes, you can jump by any number. If you jump by five from 2, you will land exactly on 7.
asks: What if I jump by three?

faq.q: Does the number line always go up to 20?
faq.a: The number line we are using today goes up to 20. We can learn numbers bigger later on.
asks: What is the biggest number on this line?

faq.q: If I order numbers, do I always start from one?
faq.a: You can order them any way, but usually, we start from the smallest number and go up to the largest one.
asks: Do I always start at the beginning?
How do I put these numbers in order?

facts: The number line shows the order of whole numbers.
Numbers increase as you move to the right on the line.
Jumping forward means adding a number.
The number before 11 is 10, and the number after 11 is 12.

quiz.say: What number is in the spot right after 13?
quiz.why: The number that comes right after 13 is 14, because we count up one space.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the number must be different from the starting number.
wrong.1: This is wrong because 15 is too far ahead; we only jump one space.
wrong.3: This is wrong because 12 is smaller than 13, so it comes before it.

quiz.say: Which group shows the numbers in the correct order?
quiz.why: When ordering numbers, we always go from the smallest number to the largest number.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you are counting backwards instead of forwards.
wrong.2: This is wrong because 12 is bigger than 11, so it must come after it.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the middle number given was 11, so we must use it.
